newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine winter wheat looks good-acting ag minister.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine winter wheat looks good-acting ag minister.

text.p: The bulk of Ukraine's winter wheat crop is growing in good condition, acting Agriculture Minister Boris Supikhanov said on Tuesday.
"This is better than at this time last year," he told parliament. "Most of the grain has wintered well, and 90 percent of the hectares sown are in very nice condition."
Ukraine sowed 7.5 million hectares to winter grain, mostly winter wheat, for harvesting this autumn.
Winter wheat accounts for the bulk of Ukraine's wheat production.
"Seven million hectares are in good and satisfactory condition," Supikhanov said. "All over the country, the volume of moisture is enough for continued good growth."
Ministry officials said last month that Ukraine needed to resow up to 500,000 hectares of frost-damaged winter wheat during the spring sowing campaign.
Supikhanov said there was enough seed for spring sowing and that the government was storing up fuel supplies.
"We also have more fertiliser and pesticides than last year," he added.
The acting minister said state and private farmers needed three billion hryvnias for spring sowing and that the government would advance 1.1-1.2 billion in direct credits.
The money would finance production and purchases of the 5.88 million tonnes of grain that the state plans to buy from the 1997 crop.

President Leonid Kuchma has yet to name a replacement for former agriculture minister Anatoly Khorishko who sacked late last month. --Yuri Kulikov, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264 ($1 = 1.8320 hryvnia )
